sampling_model.design: Fixed finite family of perfect-intervention settings \(v=(S,x)\), where \(x=0\) or a unit coordinate vector in \(\mathbb R^S\).
sampling_model.units: For the statistical rung, \(m\) independent equilibrium observations are drawn in every retained setting; population identification uses the full response kernels.
sampling_model.treatment: A treatment sets every observed coordinate in \(S\) to \(x\) and preserves the remaining equations and source laws.
sampling_model.overlap: No treatment-overlap condition is needed because regimes are designed; every retained regime has \(m\) draws.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No source separation is performed. Empirical characteristic functions at \(J_m\) computable rational frequencies are compared with globally certified compact-model characteristic functions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For irreducible latent cyclic linear non-Gaussian models, observational distribution equivalence is characterized by equality of children-basis families up to a vertex permutation.
Latent directed acyclic graphs are hard-intervention equivalent exactly when their intervention-indexed augmented maximal ancestral graphs satisfy the stated skeleton and collider criteria.
The pair condition together with the covariance condition is necessary and sufficient for full recovery of a linear cyclic model from experimental means and covariances.

Proposition 5.1 states that the observational distribution together with the atomic interventional distribution for coordinate \(i\) recovers row \(i\) of the square coefficient matrix, hence its parents and causal effects.
Aligned single-target equilibrium response maps identify a latent cyclic mechanism under full target coverage, with a graph-dependent characterization when one target is missing.
Cross-cumulant tensor rank restrictions yield goodness-of-fit tests for latent linear non-Gaussian structural equation models.
Inverting graph-indexed goodness-of-fit tests yields asymptotically valid confidence sets for causal orderings in acyclic additive-error models.

body.tldr: The paper characterizes equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets for finite latent linear non-Gaussian feedback graphs. At the exact-support level, an affine and Hall--Rado realization theorem, an unrestricted visible-source partition theorem, and simultaneous response constraints give a sound-and-complete coupled invariant and an effective sign-cell compiler. A new downward-closure theorem then proves explicitly that the zero-allowed class is the finite union of exact-support strata and gives its own finite coupled criterion; no monotone transfer of exact-support equality is assumed. Response slopes are identified as unique probability-law translations, so population identification requires neither centering nor moments. The no-latent reduction recovers row labels through atomic kernels, the exact-support four-node witness proves strict refinement over observational equivalence, and finite variance remains local to that covariance witness and the bounded-Laplace inference rung.

project_justification.gap: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. Results on latent acyclic intervention equivalence and second-order experiment design address different causal models or targets, and they do not supply the cancellation-preserving cyclic common-lift criterion required here.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a finite coupled invariant that simultaneously represents exact-support affine completion, all support subgraphs in the zero-allowed class, invisible or merged independent sources, principal intervention responses identified without moments, and common-mechanism gluing on every lower-dimensional stratum.
project_justification.fill: The exact-support theorem reduces mechanisms to graph-generated affine, rank, Hall--Rado, and principal-minor charts; a Bernoulli lattice factorization reduces unrestricted source-law containment to finite proportional-column surjections; probability-translation rigidity identifies response slopes; and simultaneous response equations enforce one mechanism across regimes. The zero-allowed extension proves \(\mathcal P^{\le}_{\mathcal I}(G)=\bigcup_{F\subseteq G}\mathcal P_{\mathcal I}(F)\) and compiles the resulting finite subgraph disjunction with an explicit size-dependent bound. The characteristic-function inference rung remains a separate compact finite-variance subclass.

body.related_work: Dai et al. characterize observational distributional equivalence for the zero-allowed LiNG class; existing results do not characterize equality of joint perfect-intervention response-kernel sets or the additional requirement that one mechanism and source tuple realize all regimes. At \(\mathcal I=\{\varnothing\}\) and fixed latent cardinality, the new zero-allowed theorem matches Dai et al.'s support convention and extends the object to common-mechanism joint interventions by an explicit finite union over exact-support subgraphs. The exact-support theorem is retained as the stratum-level engine; zero-allowed equality is proved through downward closure, not inferred by monotonicity. Zhou et al. study do-calculus invariances for latent directed acyclic graphs rather than cyclic parametric full-law sets. Bongers et al. provide surgical-intervention solvability semantics. Hyttinen, Eberhardt, and Hoyer study second-order full recovery under experiment-design conditions. Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, recover one square-model row from observational and randomized atomic-intervention distributions; the internal moment-free reduction additionally supplies the response-kernel translation lift and matching-set equality. Taeb et al. and Joint Causal Inference emphasize shared mechanisms across environments but do not prove the present cyclic non-Gaussian common-lift criterion. Bicycle supplies a perturbational gene-regulation use case, without validating linear equilibrium semantics or implying an empirical performance gain.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The affine and Hall--Rado realization criterion has passed forced-zero, latent-rank, degenerate-pivot, and exact rational witness checks at \(N=4\), but these finite checks do not prove the universal punctured-affine selection theorem. The source-partition argument still requires a full audit of finite-support measure equality in the original jump lattice and non-Gaussian closure after merging. The population compiler must handle every lower-dimensional cell and produce its own explicit complexity bound. The displayed strict-refinement witness does not establish failure of independent regime-wise equivalence; that stronger issue remains Open-ended Question 2.
body.honest_scope: The intervention pushforward identity, finite checks, and explicit witness provide proof architecture, not settled results. The sound-and-complete chart theorem, source-factorization theorem, effective compiler, common-lift boundary, internal no-latent projection, lift and matching-set equality, and statistical certification are all stated as claims to prove. Sharifian et al., Proposition 5.1, supplies only the published row-recovery comparator. The theorem is uniform over each finite input size but does not range over unbounded latent cardinality in one run. Under \(\ell=0\), the observational projection equals the square perfect-matching object, and the atomic projection restricts it by the recovered row labels. No strict-extension corollary to Dai et al.'s zero-allowed observational class is asserted because that class permits coefficient-zero strata and omits the coupled intervention object, so its graph-indexed equivalence relation is not the same ordered model-class comparison.
